title: 2026-12-22 POC weekly - latency tuning - AuroraBank

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-22 16:00 UTC | Duration: 42m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Priya (AuroraBank Lead ML Eng), Tom (Infra), Sara (Security), Ben (PM)

Summary (auto): weekly POC check-in focused on latency tuning.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, short agenda today — quick run through of the runs you sent last week, TTFT numbers, streaming behavior, and next steps.
[00:18] Priya: yeah thanks Maya, we saw the initial numbers Diego sent, um, so overall TTFT improved with streaming but p95 is still kinda high on long requests.
[00:28] Diego: right, so quick reminder, streaming on our side means we open the response stream as soon as the first token is decoded. That reduces TTFT but it can increase overall server CPU for small batches.
[00:41] Tom: the infra note is we saw spikes when sequence len > 700, our autoscaler was thrashing a bit.
[00:49] Maya: got it. Can you remind us what model variant and kernel you were running for that run?
[00:56] Priya: we were on redwood-instruct-v1 quantized 4-bit, ran on A100 cluster, standard cuBLAS kernels.
[01:04] Diego: and that's where we think kernel choice matters — flash-attn variants (custom kernels) tend to have better latency for longer seq. But cuBLAS path sometimes wins for short sequences.
[01:18] Ben: quick question — when you say TTFT are we measuring from client send to first byte on client? or server decode?
[01:25] Maya: good call — for our benchmarks TTFT is client-send to first-byte-received at the SDK level, so it includes network + first decode.
[01:33] Priya: okay that matches our measurement generally.
[01:36] [02:05] Diego: we ran a microbenchmark last week: 128/256/512/1024 sequences, batch sizes 1/4/8. On A100 cuBLAS was best at 128/256; at 512+ flash-attn saw lower p50 and p95. On H100 the custom kernel was overall better across ranges but we haven't done our full H100 runs yet.
[02:27] Tom: we have H100 dev nodes but not the full fleet — we can spin up a few but need to see the cost.
[02:34] Priya: are those runs available in the sheet? I think I saw a couple rows but not the H100 ones.
[02:40] Diego: I uploaded A100 CSV yesterday, H100 is pending. Will do H100 this week — we'll simulate the 1k sequence tail.
[02:48] Maya: also worth mentioning prefix/KV cache — we saw a 20% token compute reduction when cache hit rate was high. Priya, do you have hit rate numbers?
[02:57] Priya: yeah, for chat flows our prefix cache hit is around 65%  median but tails drop for long sessions.
[03:05] Diego: ok that explains some p95s — when KV cache cold starts we get full compute. Also streaming chunk size matters: bigger chunks reduce decoding overhead but increase TTFT.
[03:18] Ben: is there a recommended streaming window? we tried 64-token chunks and it increased TTFT for short messages.
[03:26] Diego: we usually recommend adaptive windows: emit first token asap (small chunk) then increase to 64-128 for subsequent streaming to balance TTFT vs throughput.
[03:39] [05:00] Priya: security question — Sara, any concerns about on-prem telemetry we might need to redact?
[05:07] Sara: mainly KMS and audit logs. We need to see how Redwood's private deployment handles customer-managed KMS, and whether audit logs include token-level traces.
[05:18] Maya: we can share the SOC2 whitepaper and our KMS integration doc — I'll send that after the call.
[05:23] Sara: please include retention settings for logs, and ability to disable token-level tracing.
[05:30] Diego: noted. On the performance side, one thing we spotted: kernel switching adds overhead if the runtime switches paths mid-request; better to pin kernel per route where traffic shape is stable.
[05:44] Tom: is that a runtime config? can we pin model-route to a kernel profile?
[05:49] Diego: yes, config in the dedicated/private control plane — you can pin the kernel family for a model route. We'll propose a profile.
[05:56] Priya: ok, for the next week can you run H100 tests and also a gating end-to-end with streaming enabled so we can see real TTFT?
[06:06] Diego: yep; plan is H100 microbench, then a 3-hour end-to-end run using production-like traces. We'll capture TTFT, p50/p95, and token cost.
[06:15] [07:30] Priya: note on sequence lengths: 50% of our requests are <120 tokens, but 10% are >800; that tail is what hurts p95.
[07:39] Maya: makes sense. For tails we often recommend different model variant or quant profile for long sessions — fallback to an H100-optimized variant for tail requests.
[07:50] Ben: that adds cost, how big of a delta? ballpark?
[07:55] Diego: depends — H100 with custom kernel can reduce latency by 30-50% for long seq but unit token cost may be higher. We'll quantify in the bench.
[08:05] Priya: also curious about batch size strategy — our current gateway batches by 50ms window. Is there benefit to increasing or doing dynamic batching?
[08:13] Diego: dynamic batching that adapts to request arrival rate is best; for bursty traffic 50ms may be fine but for steady low qps you want longer windows to improve utilization. But longer windows can hurt TTFT. It's a tradeoff.
[08:26] [10:00] Tom: infra ops question — what telemetry do you need to reproduce the problem? traces, system metrics?
[10:06] Diego: ideally a 1-day trace with timestamps, seq len, model route, and a sample of payloads (anonymized). Also need CPU/GPU utilization, mem and NVLink counters if possible.
[10:15] Priya: we can pull that. I'll strip content and share next Tue.
[10:21] Maya: perfect. We'll take that and run a reproduction set on H100.
[10:26] [12:00] Diego: small note: quantization profile influences kernel path too — some kernels handle int8/4-bit better; for 4-bit we saw slightly higher decode overhead on cuBLAS path.
[12:12] Priya: hmm ok — we're on 4-bit already to save cost. Should we consider mixed precision for tails?
[12:19] Diego: could be an option — e.g., keep short requests in 4-bit and long tail in 8-bit or fp16 variant for accuracy/latency. We'll include accuracy checks in bench.
[12:30] [15:00] Ben: competitor question — have any of you seen Anthropic/Bedrock do auto-kernel switching?
[15:07] Maya: some vendors have heuristics but the runtime-level control we give is more explicit — you can choose fallback policies and pin kernels per route, which helps consistency.
[15:18] Sara: for security, will kernel pinning affect patching/mitigations?
[15:23] Diego: no, kernel pinning is a config choice; patches apply to runtime. We'll document any security implications.
[15:30] [18:00] Priya: ok, next step checklist — we'll share traces, Diego will run H100 bench, Maya to send SOC2/KMS docs.
[18:10] Maya: and we'll update the shared benchmark sheet with the A100 numbers and notes. Links in chat: https://redwood.example.com/benchmarks/aurorabank-deck (note: placeholder).
[18:22] Tom: I'll coordinate the H100 node access and confirm cost center.
[18:28] [20:00] Diego: one more detail — streaming chunk strategy: emit first token at 1-2 token chunk, then switch to 64 tokens after the first 2-3 chunks to keep TTFT low but overall throughput good. We'll run that in the E2E.
[20:41] Priya: sounds good. Also want to test the prefix cache TTL behavior — we saw cache evictions at 30m that cause cold starts.
[20:52] Diego: we can tune TTL and prefetch heuristics. We'll propose settings.
[20:58] [25:00] Ben: any blockers on your side?
[25:07] Priya: main blocker is getting the anonymized traces and H100 run time. We'll try to get both by Mon/Tue.
[25:15] Maya: Redwood will prioritize the H100 bench after trace arrives.
[25:22] Diego: and we'll include accuracy regression checks when we change quant/kernel combos.
[25:30] [30:00] Action recap:
- Diego to run H100 + A100 microbench (512/1024 seq) and upload CSVs.
- Priya to share anonymized traces and seq len percentiles.
- Sara to confirm KMS/log retention policy and accept SOC2 doc.
- Maya to send security pack + benchmark link.

[31:00] Priya: can you also add cost estimates for the fallback route? we need to show PM.
[31:07] Diego: yep will add a cost column (CPU/GPU time + estimated $).
[31:12] Ben: great. If we can run the E2E week of Jan 4 that will be ideal, can you pencil that in?
[31:18] Maya: I'll send a doodle and propose Jan 4 or Jan 5 3-hour window.
[31:25] [37:00] Sara: one final ask on audit logs — need ability to exclude content from logs and still keep meta logs. Is that supported?
[37:10] Maya: yes, redact-by-default options exist in Private; we'll include details in the security doc.
[37:18] Sara: thanks.
[37:25] Maya: ok thanks everyone — we'll follow up in chat and update the sheet.
[37:30] Priya: thanks all.
[37:33] Meeting end.
